prompt: Challenge C144-CH2: Downstream purification — specifically the ultrafiltration step — runs at only 55% of nominal throughput because the membranes foul with res

content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Cross-flow ultrafiltration fouling in oil processing occurs primarily through concentration polarization and irreversible deposit accumulation, with irreversible fouling accounting for up to 45% of total membrane resistance and flux declining 65-80% within the first 30 minutes of operation.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-07415","field":"abstract","quote":"Resistance-in-series analysis attributed 55 % of total resistance to reversible concentration polarisation and 45 % to irreversible fouling"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-07415","field":"abstract","quote":"Permeate flux declined by 65–80 % within the first 30 min of operation"}]},{"text":"Spiral-wound polyethersulfone ultrafiltration modules experience quantifiable irreversible fouling after 8 hours of operation, with two-step alkaline and acid cleaning sequences restoring 94% of clean-water flux.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-07419","field":"abstract","quote":"Irreversible fouling after 8 h was quantified at 18 % flux loss; a two-step cleaning sequence restored 94 % of clean-water flux"}]},{"text":"Pretreatment and filter-aid characterization prior to membrane filtration are fundamental to minimizing downstream fouling in edible oil processing, with industrial practice emphasizing the role of solid-liquid separation staging.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-07417","field":"abstract","quote":"Coverage begins with the governing equations for constant-pressure and constant-rate dead-end filtration, including compressible cake theory and the role of filter aids"}]}],"fit":"partial","fitReason":"The researcher's publications focus on cross-flow ultrafiltration fouling mechanisms and cleaning protocols in oil processing [SYN-PUB-07419, SYN-PUB-07415], which address membrane fouling fundamentals; however, the challenge involves protease concentrate purification rather than oil processing, and the specific issue of residual whole cells and cell debris from biological fermentation differs from phospholipid fouling mechanisms in the researcher's prior work."}
